text: In the single-node delay reservoir (Appeltant 2011), how are the N virtual nodes created?
choices: By fabricating N separate physical nonlinear nodes and wiring them together
By time-multiplexing a single nonlinear node — sampling its state at N points spaced by an interval θ along the delay loop
By running N independent copies of the system in parallel
By adding N random matrices to the feedback path
explanation: One nonlinear node plus a delay loop is time-multiplexed: the delay τ is divided into N sub-intervals of width θ (τ = N·θ), and the node's state sampled at those N points becomes the N virtual-node values. This is the whole point — avoiding N physical nodes (option 0) or N parallel systems (option 2). There are no random matrices in the loop (option 3); diversity comes from the input mask.
